To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crustal and mantle contributions to the surface heat flow are highly variable from one domain to another, and the crustal contribution in the Hercynian domains of the Meseta is high due to the presence of granite intrusions.

(1) a correlation exists between the compressional seismic Pn velocity and surface heat flow and (2) the crustal contribution in the surface heat flow in Morocco is 35 m Wm−2, with high heat production values in the Hercynian domains and high mantle heat flow values in the intra-continental and Atlantic margin domains.

(1) Pn velocity is correlated with surface heat flow and the Moho temperature in Morocco; (2) the Precambrian crust is the coolest domain in Morocco; (3) high surface heat flow values are associated with thinning of the continental crust and with high crustal heat production; and (4) the Middle Atlas is a heated domain with a high mantle contribution to the surface heat flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the heat flow and the temperature distribution in the upper crust of Morocco and the geothermal regime in its major geological domains.
the thermal structure of the crust and the lithosphere in Morocco, a region that has been little investigated in terms of heat flow and geothermal modelling.
the study of the Moroccan crust and lithosphere and their thermal structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the geothermal field of the Moroccan crust is mainly controlled by the tectonic history.
the geothermal field in Morocco is controlled by the tectonic history of each geological domain, the crustal thickness, and the lithosphere thickness and age.
the geothermal field of Morocco is mainly controlled by the tectonic setting of the country.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Moroccan geothermal field is controlled by the tectonic history of the country.
the geothermal field of Morocco is controlled by both the crustal and the mantle contributions.
the geotherms and the surface heat flows are mainly controlled by the tectonic setting of the different geological domains in Morocco.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the geothermal field in Morocco is strongly affected by the geological history.
the crustal heat production is not sufficient to explain the high heat flow values in the Rif and in the Alboran Sea.
the Moroccan lithosphere is not uniform and the heat flux varies from 40 mW m–2 in some stable areas (Precambrian basement, Meseta) to 60 mW  m–2 in some extensional areas (Alboran, Rif, High Atlas).
